review.arm_blinding_assessment: PASS. build_blinded_add_record_payload() places only unit.evidence_text into payload['messages'] as a single user message. Projection label, pool_id, rollout index, trajectory SHA, acting winner SHA, and provenance are stored in r17_* fields outside messages. The score field is set to float(unit.source_score), the selected evidence trajectory verifier score, not the served acting winner score. The runner also scans rendered evidence for FORBIDDEN_VISIBLE_MARKERS and fails on leakage.
review.checkpoint_resume_assessment: PASS. Each completed arm is persisted to completed_arms.jsonl immediately after verify_completed() passes, with content-addressed receipt and skill SHAs. On resume, verify_completed() revalidates receipt/skill SHAs and contract/auth/causal-purity mode. Critically, before running an incomplete arm, the runner checks if arm_dir exists and contains any files; if so, it raises RuntimeError and stops rather than auto-rerunning.
nonblocking_notes: The adapter's module-level REQUIRED_RESOLVED_MODEL default is the historical deepseek-v4-pro-260425, but the runner always passes the fresh resolved model deepseek-v4-pro-ga-260813 explicitly, so the stale default is not exercised.

The runner's win_a/win_b pre-provider identity check is a tautological self-comparison of the same in-memory list, but the underlying evidence_units() construction is deterministic and SHA-bound, so this is acceptable.

The provider budget ledger's assert_completed_receipts_covered() helper is not called in the runner, but the runner independently asserts len(receipts) == len(claims) == result.provider_calls per arm, which covers the same invariant.
review.outcome_blind_selection_assessment: PASS. The eight pools are fixed by the predeclared lexicographic path rule in the contract's historical_inputs.selected_pools, with explicit SHA-256 bindings. The runner load_selected_pools() revalidates each pool SHA and task_id and enforces exact order, with no mixed/rescue/outcome field read before selection. No E1 held-out probe or learned-skill quality is used to select pools, model, or renderer.
review.provider_budget_assessment: PASS. ProviderBudgetLedger.claim() uses SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE and commits the claim transactionally before any provider I/O in the adapter's _respond(). Limits are 10 per arm and 30 total, bound to contract and authorization SHAs. Claims are never released, including on ambiguous failures, and are reflected in receipts via provider_budget_claim_id/unit_call_index/total_claimed_after. Parse-correction attempts and poll recovery both go through _respond(), which claims before I/O, so neither can bypass the ceiling.
